# Rich Results Test

*Tool*

Google's tool that tests a page or code snippet for structured data that can produce rich results.

**Glossary** (*Rich Results Test*): Google's tool to test and preview structured data: it shows the rich result features it detected and whether the markup is valid. It tests either a URL or a pasted code snippet.

Narrative: the topic [Implementing structured data](../topics/structured-data-implementation.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

10 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 6 shown or said at the event (1 not in Google docs, 2 confirmed by Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Rich Results Test](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7445569?hl=en).

- [`D1-C265`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Docs: Search Console Help separates critical issues, which make a structured-data item invalid and stop it from appearing as a rich result, from non-critical issues, listed under 'Improve item appearance'; the Rich Results Test reports valid items that have warnings. `[D1-C265, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7552505?hl=en]`
- [`D1-C506`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Docs: Google's Rich Results Test help says the tool tests either a page's full URL or a pasted code snippet (Code instead of URL); all page resources must be reachable by an anonymous user on the internet, so resources behind a firewall or a password are not available to the test unless exposed, for example through a tunnel. `[D1-C506, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7445569?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C515`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Slide, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google's planned validation workflow has five steps: download the rules from the feature guide, generate the JSON or embedded microdata or RDFa, run the rules against the generated server-side markup as a first check, deploy and test in the Rich Results Test, and monitor ongoing performance in Search Console. `[D2-C515, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C176`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: To check whether JavaScript content is affected, open the URL Inspection tool in Search Console or the Rich Results Test and look for that content in the rendered HTML tab. `[D2-C176, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C498`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google recommends testing and previewing structured data in the Rich Results Test, which shows the rich result features it detected and whether the markup is valid. `[D2-C498, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C501`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: A community demo's script used both input modes of Google's Rich Results Test: the URL mode for public pages, which Google fetches itself, and the code mode, into which the script pasted the page's HTML, for private pages and pages Google cannot fetch (best reading of a largely unintelligible recording; the second kind of page was heard as 'dead', possibly 'dev'). `[D1-C501, stage, a community speaker, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C502`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: In a community demo, the structured-data problems Google's Rich Results Test reported on the test page included an empty name, a breadcrumb problem and a price of zero, with errors shown in pink and warnings in orange (best readings of a largely unintelligible recording; each item is heard in only one of the two recordings). `[D1-C502, stage, a community speaker, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C249`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community demo showed a script that opens Chrome with a saved session, pastes a URL into Google's Rich Results Test, waits about 15 seconds, then screenshots and saves the result and retries on failure (the demo's recording is largely unintelligible; the tool name is a best reading). `[D1-C249, stage, a community speaker, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C240`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: Because Web Fragments monkey-patches core browser APIs such as document, history and location, test pages that use it in Google's rendering (the rendered HTML in Search Console's URL Inspection tool or the Rich Results Test), not only in a normal desktop browser. `[D2-C240, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C504`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Analysis: Audit CMS templates for duplicate markup by running one page per template through the Rich Results Test and checking whether an SEO plug-in and a theme or events plug-in emit the same type twice; 'more markup never hurts' covers relevant, non-duplicated markup only. `[D2-C504, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-SDA-06` **SHOULD** · Said at Search Central Live: Emit each structured data entity once per page, and audit CMS plug-ins for duplicates (1 of its claims mentions it)
- `DEV-SDA-08` **SHOULD** · Documented: Mark up merchant listings completely, with validity dates for sale prices (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SDA-11` **MUST** · Documented: Validate markup in the Rich Results Test before it reaches templates, and monitor it after release (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
